summary: Egress IP rotation causing residency mismatch alerts and p95 latency spike
description: Customer reports that on 2026-03-09 they began receiving audit alerts from their compliance tooling indicating outbound connections leaving the EU. Concurrently their application observed P95 latency spikes from 220ms baseline to ~1.8s for inference calls. Customer suspects residency pinning is not honouring their strict EU residency setting and that egress IPs appear to 'bounce' across regions, triggering both compliance alarms and higher round-trip times.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer account configured with strict data residency: eu-only. 2) Run sustained inference load (50 rps) against customer-specific project in production eu-west. 3) Observe audit logs for connections, check service response times and Redwood route decisions. 4) Compare egress IPs reported by customer firewall with Redwood egress allocation table.

investigation_notes:
- Initial traces show routing decision changed on a per-request basis; not a full-region failover.
- Hypothesis A: Egress IP rotation for ephemeral pools caused NAT egress to appear from us-east addresses when requests were routed to a compatible fallback pool.
- Hypothesis B: Residency check runs at request start, but later in the pipeline a caching/worker layer uses different outbound proxies for KV/cache warmup traffic, triggering customer's firewall.
- Reviewed route decision logs: a small subset (~2.3% of requests) were routed to us-east due to a temporary capacity deficit in eu-west serving pool at 14:09 UTC. Fallback policy picked a compatible model instance in us-east.
- Checked pin TTL behavior: customer's project had a pin TTL of 0 (strict), but health-checked capacity signal allowed short-lived cross-region fallback under controller policy. Current controller policy should respect strict pins; evidence shows edge-case where pre-flight capacity probe returned stale capacity leading to fallback selection.
- No changes to customer's config were detected. No code changes on customer side.
- Correlated infra maintenance windows: scheduled GPU driver update in eu-west started at 14:05 UTC, temporarily reducing available capacity in pool eu-west-gpu-1.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Maya Chen (Support): Received incident from customer. Captured logs and requested full audit trail and sample requests.

2026-03-10 10:00 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Reproduced p95 spike in internal load test with simulated degraded eu-west pool. Observed fallback to us-east for ~2.3% of requests when strict pin enforcement intersected with autoscaler cooldown window.

2026-03-11 16:25 - Compliance Engineer (Customer): Our firewall only allows egress from the 18.205.0.0/16 block. When we saw 3.124.* addresses the audit triggered. Need assurance data doesn't leave EU under strict pin.

2026-03-12 08:40 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Implemented temporary mitigation to avoid cross-region routing while strict residency flag is set. Noted as 2-step fix: short-term policy toggle + follow-up controller fix.
2026-03-12 11:02 - Support: Customer verified no new alerts after toggle; latency returned to baseline; awaiting postmortem for permanent fix.
resolution:
Short-term: Disabled cross-region fallback for projects with strict residency flag until controller fix deploys. Customer confirmed no further audit alerts and p95 returned to baseline.
Long-term: Engineering will change controller capacity-check logic to use strongly-consistent capacity view for strict residency projects and add an explicit egress-IP stickiness guarantee during pin TTL. Also: add a monitoring alert for any egress IPs observed outside allowed CIDR for strict residency projects. Expected rollout: staging validation 2026-03-18, prod deploy 2026-03-22.
Follow-ups: create runbook entry for compliance escalations, update docs clarifying behavior during scheduled maintenance, and notify customers with strict residency about planned maintenance impact windows.
